concepts.meaning: Postgres record for a seller's pay-per-click sponsored listing campaign, owned by this domain.
Postgres record of an hourly billing run that charges shops for ad clicks.
Signed value in the ad click URL that proves the click came from a served ad.
A paid product placement; up to three are served per category.
Short affiliate URL with a code, stored in DynamoDB, that redirects to a marketplace page.
Event published on each share-link redirect; consumed by a projector that stores clicks in ClickHouse.

gotchas: The ad click endpoint always redirects the user to the product, even when fraud checks reject the click. Rejection only affects counting and billing.
Ad clicks are not billed inline. They go through Kafka, then per-minute aggregation, then the hourly `ads.bill-hour` job.
Hourly billing is only approximate. `ads.reconcile-day` fixes it later from the raw click log, so numbers can shift after the fact.
Share-link clicks are stored asynchronously: redirect, then Kafka, then a projector, then ClickHouse. Stats can lag behind real clicks.
Links live in DynamoDB and click aggregates in ClickHouse, not Postgres. Only `AdCampaign` and `AdBillingRun` are Postgres tables here.
out.purpose: The marketing domain handles money-making and growth features: sellers run pay-per-click sponsored listings, and users create affiliate short links. It tracks and bills ad clicks and attributes link clicks.

startHere.why: HTTP entry points for campaigns, sponsored listings and ad click redirects.
Core ad logic: campaigns, serving and click handling.
Signed ad click token creation and verification.
Per-minute exactly-once click counting from Kafka.
Creating, resolving and tracking share links.

out.summary: This unit has two halves. In **Sponsored ad campaigns and serving**, sellers create pay-per-click campaigns, shoppers see up to three sponsored listings per category, and each listing links to a signed redirect with daily spend counted in Redis. **Ad click tokens and fraud checks** covers `GET /ads/click/:token`: it verifies the token, filters fraud in Redis, always redirects to the product, and publishes the click to Kafka. **Aggregating and billing ad clicks** then counts those clicks per minute with exactly-once Kafka transactions, bills shops hourly through the ledger (`ads.bill-hour`), and corrects the totals daily from the raw click log (`ads.reconcile-day`). The share-link half starts with **Creating and resolving share links**: logged-in users make short affiliate links, and `GET /l/:code` 302-redirects anyone to a marketplace page. **Link click attribution and stats** closes the loop. Each redirect emits `link.clicked` to Kafka, a projector writes it to ClickHouse, and the owner reads 7-day per-minute counts from `GET /links/:code/stats`.

concepts.meaning: A balanced set of double-entry `LedgerEntry` rows posted together; entries are immutable.
Event emitted in the same transaction as a journal; the balance projection consumes it.
A payment whose Stripe outcome is unclear; a job later resolves it by idempotency key.
Key sent to Stripe so a charge happens once; also used to match payments during reconciliation.
On `order.paid`, net amount (total minus platform fee) is split across shops and credited in the ledger.
A weekly transfer of a shop's balance, created by `payouts.run-weekly` and sent by `payouts.send`.

gotchas: Balances come from a Redis projection fed by `ledger.journal_posted`, so they can lag the ledger.
Ledger entries are immutable; corrections, such as payout reversals, are new journals, not edits.
Payouts are two steps: `payouts.run-weekly` moves money in the ledger, then `payouts.send` calls Stripe. The ledger is reversed only if Stripe definitely refuses.
Payments stuck in UNKNOWN are not failures; `payments.resolve-unknown` settles them through the ledger so orders react normally.
The domain both publishes and consumes `ledger.journal_posted`, so check for loops when you change the listeners.
out.purpose: The payments domain takes card payments through Stripe, records every money movement in a double-entry ledger, credits shops when orders are paid, and pays shops out weekly through Stripe Connect.

startHere.why: Core of the domain: posts balanced journals and emits the event.
Charges the card via Stripe and handles the payment flow.
Credits shops in the ledger when an order is paid.
Weekly payout creation and sending jobs.
Builds the Redis shop balance from ledger journals.

out.summary: A buyer's payment request arrives on the `payments.requests` topic, and "Charging a card through Stripe" charges the card once and saves the result using the "Payment records and DTO service". If a payment ends up stuck, "Resolving payments stuck in UNKNOWN" asks Stripe what really happened, and "Daily Stripe reconciliation" double-checks our records against Stripe every night. When an order is paid, "Settling paid orders to shops" credits each shop's share, and it does this through "Recording money in the ledger". The ledger event feeds "Shop balance and payout history reads", which serve balances from Redis. "Weekly seller payouts" then turns balances into `Payout` rows and sends them via Stripe Connect. "Ledger partitions and invariant checks" keeps the ledger healthy by creating partitions and checking that entries sum to zero.
